name: MinimumDailyVolumeFilter
quote: It is relatively easy to look for swings in high-volume stocks (at least three million shares per day, but preferably seven million or more)...
description: Only take swing setups in a symbol whose (daily) bar volume exceeds a minimum threshold.
book_order_type: n/a (symbol/context filter, not an order placement)
notes: Unlike VolumeAboveAverageMultiple (relative to the symbol's own rolling average), this is an absolute share-count threshold intended for daily bars/symbol selection.

name: HugeVolumeCapitulationReversal
quote: When a stock is in a steep bear trend on the daily chart and then has a day with volume that is five to 10 times its recent average, the bulls may have capitulated and a tradable bottom may be present... if it has a strong bull close, the odds of a profitable long increase.
description: In a steep bear trend on the daily chart, a bar whose volume is a large multiple of its recent average and which closes as a strong bull (trend) bar signals capitulation and a tradable bottom for a swing long.
pseudocode: volume[0] >= volumeMultiple * average(volume, n)[1] && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
book_order_type: buy at the close of the huge-volume bull bar, or more cautiously on a stop above its high

complexity.reason: combines an N-bar average-volume ratio with a trend-bar body test and an implicit prior-bear-trend context

notes: Composes VolumeAboveAverageMultiple-style volume ratio with the BullReversalBarShape-style trend-bar primitive from Chapter 2; a prior-bear-trend context gate is assumed but not defined here.
Brooks expects at least a two-legged move to the moving average to follow, which is a separate exit/target idea, not captured as its own candidate here.
chapter_title: Huge Volume Reversals on Daily Charts

name: HugeVolumeBarIntraday
quote: On a 1 minute Emini chart that is in a strong bear trend, if there is a huge volume bar (about 25,000 contracts), it is unlikely to be the end of the bear trend, but often is a sign that a pullback will come soon.
description: Primitive: the current bar's volume exceeds an absolute huge-volume threshold (illustrated at about 25,000 contracts on the 1 minute Emini) - flags a bar as a volume-climax candidate within a strong intraday bear trend.
book_order_type: n/a (context flag, not itself an order)
notes: Absolute-contract-count threshold is instrument-specific (illustrated for the Emini); would need rescaling for other markets.
Brooks explicitly warns volume is unreliable intraday on the 5 minute chart he otherwise recommends for trading - kept for recall, confidence medium/low on usefulness.

name: MinimumDailyVolumeForDayTradingEligibility
quote: If the stock is not one that you normally trade intraday but its volume is about five million shares or more, it is worth considering adding it to your basket of day trading stocks for a day or two.
description: Only consider a stock eligible for intraday trading if its recent daily volume is at least a minimum share count.
book_order_type: n/a (a pre-trade eligibility filter, evaluated on the daily bar)
notes: rules/CATALOG.md's volume rules (VolumeBelowAverage, VolumeAboveAverageMultiple) test volume relative to its own recent average; this is an absolute share-count floor, a different and simpler test.

name: ShavedBarLowVolumeFilter
quote: When the market is quiet and the volume is low, shaved tops and bottoms are sometimes common and are not a sign of strength... Each of those bars is a trap.
description: Blocks ShavedBarEntry when several shaved bars have clustered in the recent bars and this bar's volume is below its own average -- a sign of a quiet, low-volume trading range rather than genuine strength.
pseudocode: countIf(k = 0..clusterLookback-1, ShavedBar[k] (either side)) >= clusterCountMin && volume[0] <= volumeFraction * average(volume, volAvgLookback)

complexity.reason: a windowed count plus a volume-average comparison

notes: Brooks ties this to volume being 'low' without a number; the volume-average test is this pass's reading of that.
